test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Under the Zabt system of Mughal empire, how was tax determined?

options.text: Based on crop yields, prices and area cultivated
Based on fixed percentage of the crop yield
Based on fixed annual amount per farmer

solution:
The correct answer is __**Based on crop yields, prices and area cultivated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Zabt system** was a significant land revenue system introduced during the reign of the **Mughal Emperor Akbar**. It was primarily developed and implemented by his finance minister, **Raja Todar Mal**, around the year **1580**.
 
• Under this system, the **revenue** was determined after a very careful survey of **crop yields**, **market prices**, and the **area of land cultivated** over a continuous period of **ten years** (from **1570 to 1580**).
 
• Each crop had its own schedule of revenue rates, known as **Dastur-i-Amal**. The state's share was generally fixed at **one-third** of the average produce, which was converted into **cash** based on prevailing market prices. ***Hence, the statement that tax was determined based on crop yields, prices, and area cultivated is correct.***
 
• The **Zabt system** was applied in those provinces where the Mughal administration could carry out land surveys and maintain detailed accounts, such as **Delhi**, **Agra**, **Awadh**, **Allahabad**, **Malwa**, and **Lahore**.
 
• It was also known as the **Dahshala system** because it relied on the average statistics of **ten years** (Dah meaning ten) to provide stability to both the state and the cultivators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Land:** For the purpose of revenue assessment under **Akbar**, land was divided into four categories based on the continuity of cultivation:

 
 
• **Polaj**: Land which was annually cultivated for each crop in succession and never allowed to lie fallow.
 
• **Parauti**: Land left out of cultivation for a time (**1 or 2 years**) that it might recover its strength.
 
• **Chachar**: Land that had lain fallow for **3 or 4 years**.
 
• **Banjar**: Land uncultivated for **5 years** or more.
 
 
 
• **Land Measurement:** To ensure precision, **Akbar** replaced the old hempen rope with a new measuring unit called the **Gaj-i-Ilahi** (a yard of **41 digits** or about **33 inches**) and used a **Tanab** (measuring chain) made of **Bamboo** sticks joined by iron rings.
 
• **Administrative Officers:** The collection was overseen by officials such as the **Amalguzar** (revenue collector) and the **Bitikchi** (accountant). At the local level, the **Kanungo** maintained the records of **area cultivated** and **local prices**.
 
• **Geographical Limitations:** The **Zabt** system could not be implemented in provinces like **Gujarat** and **Bengal** because the administration found it difficult to conduct regular surveys and keep track of fluctuating **crop yields** in those terrains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cash Collection:** Unlike earlier systems where revenue was often paid in kind, the **Zabt system** prioritized collection in **cash**. This necessitated the expansion of **local markets** and the **monetization** of the rural economy.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal:** Before serving **Akbar**, **Raja Todar Mal** had worked under **Sher Shah Suri**, where he gained initial experience in land measurement and revenue reforms, which he later perfected during the **Mughal era**.
 
• **Impact on Peasants:** While the system brought transparency, the requirement to pay in **cash** often forced peasants to sell their produce immediately after harvest, sometimes at lower prices, to meet the state's **revenue demand**.
 
• **Mansabdari Link:** The revenue collected through the **Zabt system** was used to pay the salaries of the **Mansabdars** and maintain the massive military machinery of the **Mughal Empire**.
